This vignette fuses a trial with one observational data set to estimate
a CATE, using the frugal parametrisation from `causl`.

## The four blocks

Let $C$ be baseline covariates (including effect modifiers), $Z$ further
pre-treatment variables, $X$ the treatment and $Y$ the outcome. The
frugal factorisation is

$$p(c)\;p(z\mid c)\;p(x\mid z,c)\;q(y\mid do(x),c),
\quad\text{with a copula linking } z \text{ and } y.$$

The outcome margin $q(y\mid do(x),c)$ is the law of $Y$ under an
intervention on $X$; its coefficients are the causal effect. For MDPL
you supply three of the four blocks as one flat list of formulas:

| block | models | what to put in it |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 1\. `Z` | pre-treatment variables $p(z\mid c)$ | one formula per variable, e.g. `Z ~ C1`. Nuisance: keep it simple. |
| 2\. `X` | treatment and covariate margins | used to **generate** data only; left out of the fit. |
| 3\. `Y` | the causal margin $q(y\mid do(x),c)$ | **the causal block.** `X`, interacted with each modifier the CATE depends on (`Y ~ X * C1`). No `Z` here. |
| 4\. `cop` | dependence between the margins | a one-sided formula (`~ 1`, `~ X * C1`). Nuisance, but it does the adjustment for $Z$. |

So the specification is

```{r spec}
spec <- mdpl_causl(
  formulas = list(
    Z ~ C1,        # block 1
    Y ~ X * C1,    # block 3: CATE terms Y:X and Y:C1:X
    ~ X * C1       # block 4
  ),
  family = c(1, 1, 1),
  outcome = "Y",
  kwd = "cop"
)
spec
```

and the CATE is the outcome margin's linear predictor at $X=1$ minus
$X=0$, $\tau(c_1)=\beta_X+\beta_{X:C_1}c_1$. Only the outcome block
enters it; the `Z` and copula blocks sharpen and de-bias those two
coefficients. `family` is one code per formula (`1` Gaussian, `5`
binary; the last is the copula).

## A simulated example

The trial ($n_e=250$) is randomised. The observational data ($n_o=1000$)
are confounded by a binary $U$ that affects both treatment and outcome
and is dropped before analysis. The true CATE is $\tau(c_1)=0.8+0.3c_1$.
The generator needs all four blocks, including a treatment model.

```{r sim}
set.seed(11)
n_e <- 250; n_o <- 1000
family <- list(1, c(5, 1, 5), 1, 1)   # families for blocks Z, (X, C1, U), Y, copula

forms_obs <- list(
  Z ~ C1,
  list(X ~ Z * C1 + U, C1 ~ 1, U ~ 1),
  Y ~ X * C1 + U,
  ~ X * C1
)
forms_exp <- forms_obs
forms_exp[[2]][[1]] <- X ~ 1                      # randomised

pars_obs <- list(
  C1 = list(beta = 0, phi = 1),
  U = list(beta = 0),
  Z = list(beta = c(0.2, 0.6), phi = 1),
  X = list(beta = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.1, 1, 0.4)),       # U drives treatment
  Y = list(beta = c(0.6, 0.8, 0.2, 1, 0.3), phi = 2),
  cop = list(beta = matrix(c(1, 2.5, 0, 0), nrow = 4))
)
pars_exp <- pars_obs; pars_exp$X <- list(beta = 0)

d_o <- causl::rfrugalParam(
  n = n_o,
  formulas = forms_obs,
  family = family,
  pars = pars_obs
)
d_e <- causl::rfrugalParam(
  n = n_e,
  formulas = forms_exp,
  family = family,
  pars = pars_exp
)
d_o$U <- d_e$U <- NULL                            # U is not observed
head(d_e, 3)
```

The analysis uses only `Z`, `C1`, `X` and `Y`.

## MDPL Fitting

```{r fit}
system.time(
  fit <- mdpl(
    model = spec,
    data_exp = d_e,
    data_obs = list(obs = d_o),
    treat = "X"
  )
)
fit
```

This fits both data sets, chooses the weight and builds the posterior.
The coefficients of the two fits:

```{r pars}
round(cbind(trial = fit$fit_exp$par, observational = fit$fit_obs[[1]]$par), 3)
```

`Y:X` and `Y:C1:X` are $\beta_X$ and $\beta_{X:C_1}$ (truth 0.8 and
0.3). The rest (`Z:*`, `cop*`, `phi:*`) is nuisance. The weight is
judged on all parameters by default; `target = "cate"` judges it on the
two treatment-effect parameters only.

## CATE and ATE

The table compares three estimates of the CATE at $C_1=-1,0,1$: the
trial alone (`fit$rct`), MDPL, and a pooled fit that takes the
observational data at full weight (`eta = 1`). `mdpl_cate()` returns the
estimate, standard error and interval for each, and `truth` is the known
$0.8+0.3c_1$.

```{r cate}
g <- data.frame(C1 = c(-1, 0, 1))
pooled <- mdpl_posterior(fit$fit_exp, fit$fit_obs, eta = 1, treat = "X")   # eta = 1
tab <- rbind(
  cbind(method = "trial only", mdpl_cate(fit$rct, g, treat = "X")),
  cbind(method = "MDPL",       mdpl_cate(fit, g)),
  cbind(method = "pooled",     mdpl_cate(pooled, g)))
tab$truth <- 0.8 + 0.3 * tab$C1
tab[, c("method", "C1", "estimate", "se", "lower", "upper", "truth")]
```

The plot draws the same three CATE curves over a grid of $C_1$ values,
with intervals for the trial and MDPL (the pooled interval is omitted
for legibility) and the true CATE dashed.

```{r cate-plot}
cg <- data.frame(C1 = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 41))
cs <- list(trial = mdpl_cate(fit$rct, cg, treat = "X"),
           mdpl = mdpl_cate(fit, cg),
           pooled = mdpl_cate(pooled, cg))
cols <- c(trial = "grey40", mdpl = "#0072B2", pooled = "#D55E00")
plot(NA, xlim = c(-2, 2), ylim = c(-0.5, 2.2), xlab = expression(C[1]),
     ylab = expression(tau(C[1])))
for (nm in names(cs)) {
  if (nm != "pooled")
    polygon(c(cg$C1, rev(cg$C1)), c(cs[[nm]]$lower, rev(cs[[nm]]$upper)),
            col = adjustcolor(cols[nm], 0.15), border = NA)
  lines(cg$C1, cs[[nm]]$estimate, col = cols[nm], lwd = 2)
}
abline(0.8, 0.3, lty = 2, lwd = 2)
legend("topleft", c("truth", "trial only", "MDPL", "pooled"),
       col = c("black", cols), lty = c(2, 1, 1, 1), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
```

The ATE averages the CATE over the covariates of a data frame (by
default the trial's). The code below gives it for the same three
methods, then prints the true value over the trial covariates for
comparison:

```{r ate}
rbind(`trial only` = mdpl_ate(fit$rct, d_e, treat = "X"),
      MDPL = mdpl_ate(fit),
      pooled = mdpl_ate(pooled, d_e))
cat("true ATE over the trial covariates:", round(0.8 + 0.3 * mean(d_e$C1), 3), "\n")
```

Pooling (`eta = 1`) takes the observational estimates at face value;
MDPL borrows only as much as the trial supports. The bootstrap
(`bootstrap_CI = TRUE`, see the intervals vignette) refits both models
per replicate, which with `causl` is slow.

Note: if you have several observational data sets, pass a list of data
frames; each gets its own weight and is fitted separately.

Also, **`target = "cate"`** picks up every outcome-block coefficient
involving `X`, including further modifiers.
